summary: Hiroshi Aoyagi is a scholar in linguistics and Japanology. He studied at International Christian University (~1980–1986) and completed his PhD at the University of Southern California (~1991–1998). Around 2004, he held a professorship at Nanzan University.

Hiroshi Araki works in Japanology and Buddhist studies, having earned degrees including a PhD from Kyoto University (~1978–2013). His academic career includes posts at Osaka University (1992, 2006) and a professorship at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (2010–2025).
Hiroshi Deguchi studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1952). He held an academic post at Hokkaido University between approximately 1957 and 1963.
Hiroshi Kanaseki was a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at Kyoto University from ~1948 to 1951. He later served in a post at Tenri University from ~1981 to 1998.

Hiroshi Kanno specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology, having studied at the University of Tokyo (~1972–1984). He served as Director at Soka University (1997) and at the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology (~2001–2009).

Hiroshi Kuroda is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University (~1974–1976). He served as an associate professor at Osaka Gakuin University (attested 1983–1990) and Osaka Gakuin Junior College (attested 1988).

Hiroshi Marui, a scholar of Indology and philosophy, studied at the University of Tokyo (BA 1972–1983, PhD 2011), Pune University, and under Albrecht Wezler. He served as associate professor at the University of Tokyo (1992, 1995, 1999–2018).
Hiroshi Maruyama is an Indology scholar who served as a professor at Osaka University and led the Ayurveda Research Society, both attested in 1987.
Hiroshi Nemoto is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his MA at Hiroshima University, where he also held a professorship (attested 2015–2016).

Hiroshi Yamashita works in Indology and religious studies. He studied as an international student at the University of Madras and served as an associate professor at Tohoku University (attested 1996–1999).
Hirotomo Teranishi succeeded Hiroshi Kanno in 2009 and served as a director at Soka University (attested 2010–2011).
Hiroyuki Kato was a scholar in philosophy who held posts at Bansho Shirabesho (~1860–1862), Kaisei School (~1869–1877), and the University of Tokyo (~1877–1893).
Hisanosuke Izui was a linguistics scholar who studied at Kyoto University from ~1927 to 1930. He later held an academic post at Kyoto Sangyo University from ~1969 to 1978.

Hisao Inagaki specialized in Buddhist studies, earning degrees from Kobe City University of Foreign Studies, Ryukoku University, and the University of London (PhD 1968). He taught at SOAS (1969–1981) and served as professor at Ryukoku University (1981–1998).

Hisao Kanaseki, active in Buddhist studies, studied at Doshisha University (~1939–1942). He held professorships at Kobe University (~1966–1974) and Komazawa University (~1982–1993), and was professor emeritus at Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1974–1982).

Hisao Takahashi is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University (~1970–1974) under Ryukai Mano. His career at Taisho University included roles as assistant (attested 1977–1982), lecturer (~1987–1996), and professor (~2002–2015).

Hisashi Matsumura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post at Australian National University (attested 1982) and served as an associate professor at Kobe Shinwa University (attested 1996).

Hisashi Sato was a Tibetology and history scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1935–1938), later becoming professor there in 1968. He also held posts at Bukkyo University (~1977–1984), Komazawa University, and Toyo University.

Hisataka Ishida specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his doctorate from the University of Vienna (2011) under Helmut Krasser, later serving as lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 2015).

Hisatake Kato studied philosophy at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1967). His academic posts included the University of Tokyo (~1967–1972), Yamagata University (~1972–1980), Tohoku University (~1980–1992), Tottori University of Environmental Studies (~2001–2005), and the University of Human Arts and Sciences (~2005–2009).
